A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the loggerhead population in the western North Atlantic is large and stable, but that there is a high level of uncertainty associated with population estimates.

we developed a novel approach to estimate adult female loggerhead populations that includes uncertainty, and that we provide a new estimate of the western North American population of 38 334 adult females (95% confidence limits: 30 000�50 000 adult females).
our results suggest that a population of 38 334 females is not large enough to support the population growth necessary to recover the loggerhead turtle.
The main takeaway from our work is that
uncertainty in population estimates should not be ignored, and should be explicitly considered in the evaluation of population status and management.
the uncertainty associated with the estimate of the number of adult female turtles is much larger than the uncertainty associated with estimates of the number of nests.

a single point estimate of adult population size is insufficient for evaluating population status and for making management decisions, as it does not convey the range of uncertainty associated with the estimate.
